pathway.title: Accendra Health Inc/Va/ — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: Leverage is high and rising on current earnings. Net debt is 8.05x calculated reported EBITDA and 6.74x issuer-adjusted EBITDA for the last twelve months, against 4.72x adjusted at the end of 2025, and 9.04x on adjusted EBITDA annualised from the third quarter. Net debt fell only 2.24% since 2025-12-31 while adjusted EBITDA fell 41.64% in nine months. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ach_ach-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 31; calculation C01; calculation C05; calculation C09; calculation C10; calculation C26

Cash interest is about to step up. The 2032 first lien and 2033 second lien notes pay their first coupons on 2026-12-15 and carry USD 116.59 million of fixed cash interest a year, which is 90.55% of the cash interest paid on all debt in the last twelve months, while interest paid in the third quarter was 64.15% lower than a year earlier because the first coupons on the new notes fall after the quarter (an inference). At the third-quarter run-rate, issuer-defined free cash flow before interest paid is USD 66.81 million a year, so after those coupons it is negative USD 49.79 million, before any interest on the term loan and revolver. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ach_ach-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ach_ach-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ach_ach-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 31; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ach_ach-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 32; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C12; calculation C13; calculation C14; calculation C15

Debt investors already price distress at the junior tier. The issuer's own estimated fair value of total debt is 68.53% of carrying value, the first lien notes due 2032 are at 88.29%, the Term Loan B at 90.28% and the second lien notes due 2033 at 36.21% (35.81% of principal), which suggests a market view of high default risk that the carrying-value ratios do not show (an inference). On the estimated fair value of debt, net leverage would be 5.48x calculated EBITDA, a sensitivity and not the primary ratio. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ach_ach-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ach_ach-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 16; calculation C28; calculation C29

Revenue durability is the weakest business factor. Two commercial payors were 23% and 14% of 2025 revenue, the terminated contracts were 12% and explain 97.49% of the nine-month decline of 10.24%, and the same payor still accounted for about 11 percentage points of 2025 revenue outside the terminated contracts (an inference from rounded shares). The underlying trend is milder: the issuer's listed drivers outside the terminated contracts and a sold non-core asset sum to a third-quarter decline of 1.06%, and revenue from Medicare grew 4.87% while commercial payor revenue fell 13.52% and capitation revenue fell 78.02%. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_ach_omi-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 24; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ach_ach-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ach_ach-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ach_ach-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 27; calculation C16; calculation C17; calculation C30; calculation C32

Margins fall faster than costs can be cut. Adjusted EBITDA fell by 56.40% of the revenue lost in nine months 2026, the adjusted margin was 7.94% in the third quarter against 13.22% a year earlier, and cost of net revenue rose to 56.4% of revenue from 52.9% because equipment depreciation is largely fixed and collection rates are lower; rental revenue fell 20.00% while equipment depreciation fell only 3.3%, so depreciation rose to 22.59% of rental revenue from 18.68%. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ach_ach-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ach_ach-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 28; calculation C09; calculation C11; calculation C27; calculation C31

Liquidity is adequate for twelve months but thin against the debt. Cash and the undrawn revolver are 15.08% of total debt and cover the run-rate free cash flow shortfall several times before term loan interest, no debt falls due before 2029 except the revolver borrowings, and the receivables programme runs to October 2029, but USD 311 million of claims sit outside total debt and the programme is 90.67% used. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ach_ach-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 37; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ach_ach-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 38; calculation C08; calculation C14; calculation C19; calculation C20; calculation C34

Refinancing capacity depends on stabilising earnings before the 2028 and 2029 dates. The Term Loan B of USD 511 million falls due in March 2029, the revolver can spring forward to December 2028, and the secured notes due in 2032 and 2033 are 69.21% of contractual principal, so the next refinancing will be tested against the third-quarter run-rate, not the 2025 results. Equity is a USD 568.23 million deficit under two NYSE notices and goodwill is 59.08% of total assets, which narrows the alternatives to another exchange or an equity issue. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ach_ach-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ach_ach-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ach_ach-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ach_ach-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 37; calculation C18; calculation C21; calculation C33

Governance adds risk but not extraction. Business & governance rates sponsor and governance risk Medium: no dividend, repurchases stopped, nearly all unsecured notes exchanged into secured notes, a new chief executive from 2026-10-05 and no controlling holder identified. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A)

A second payor loss is the downside that would break the credit. Losing revenue equal to the 14% payor share at the observed flow-through would remove about USD 218.09 million from adjusted EBITDA and leave cash and the revolver covering about 11.9 months of the resulting cash burn before any management action (an illustrative sensitivity, not a forecast). Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C11; calculation C22; calculation C23

cells.text: Accendra Health, Inc. (formerly Owens & Minor, Inc.), a Virginia corporation listed on the NYSE as ACH; one operating and reporting segment

Leading nationwide provider of home healthcare equipment, medical supplies and related services under the Apria and Byram Healthcare brands: diabetes treatment, home respiratory therapy, sleep apnea treatment, ostomy, wound care, urology and other products

Fee-for-service and capitation arrangements with government and commercial payors for equipment rented and supplies sold to patients and home health agencies; capitation is nearly all in the terminated commercial contracts
Diabetes 31.49%; Sleep therapy 24.99%; Home respiratory therapy 15.05%; Ostomy 8.80%; Wound care 6.58%; Urology 4.87%; Other 8.22% of net revenue of USD 1,842.789 million

Two largest commercial payors 23% and 14% of net revenue; Medicare and state Medicaid 19%; terminated commercial contracts USD 322 million or 12% of net revenue, including USD 231 million of capitation revenue
Net revenue -10.24% (USD -210.276 million); sleep therapy -16.2%, home respiratory therapy -14.8%, wound care -14.3%, other -30.0%; diabetes 0.1%, ostomy 4.9%, urology 4.6%
Cost of net revenue 56.4% of net revenue (52.9% in nine months 2025), selling, general and administrative 40.6% (38.8%), patient service equipment depreciation USD 92.162 million (USD 95.260 million)

Capital expenditure USD 131 million in nine months 2026 (USD 153 million in nine months 2025), mostly patient service equipment; USD 125 million of equipment sale proceeds in nine months 2026, USD 85 million tied to the payor termination
Three largest suppliers 16%, 14% and 11% of equipment and supplies purchases, about 40% in total
Over 250 locations, centers of excellence by mail-order product category, regional distribution and repair centers, a national pharmacy and a biomedical repair center
National and regional providers including AdaptHealth, Lincare, Inogen, Viemed, Quipt, Cardinal Health and Rotech; pharmacy benefit managers also compete
Medicare and Medicaid participation, Medicare competitive bidding for durable medical equipment, and Apria's Corporate Integrity Agreement, closure expected in 2026
Receivables sold on a limited-recourse basis up to USD 150 million; USD 136 million of sold receivables uncollected at 2026-09-30

runs.text: Strength one is a maturity profile with no near-term wall. The 2029 maturities are USD 511.338 million, the secured notes mature in 2032 and 2033, and only the USD 35 million of revolver borrowings fall due before 2029, so refinancing risk before then is limited to the springing revolver date. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ach_ach-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 18; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C18

Strength two is liquidity that can fund a year of base-case needs. Cash plus the undrawn revolver are 15.08% of total debt and the receivables programme was extended to October 2029, which lowers the chance of a funding gap before earnings stabilise. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ach_ach-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 23; calculation C08

Strength three is a category base that is stable. Diabetes, ostomy and urology were 45.16% of nine-month revenue and grew or held while sleep therapy and home respiratory therapy absorbed the payor loss, so the revenue floor is higher than the headline decline suggests. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ach_ach-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 27; calculation C24

Strength four is reporting that lets creditors monitor. The auditor gave unqualified opinions, disclosure controls were effective at 2026-09-30 and dated events are disclosed, which supports early warning from the triggers below. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A)

Strength five is a cost response already under way. Selling, general and administrative cost fell 6.0% and payor transitions were completed in the first half of 2026, so the base is visible. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ach_ach-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ach_ach-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 28

Weakness one is payor concentration. Two commercial payors were 23% and 14% of 2025 revenue and the terminated contracts were 12%, so one decision by a buyer with a successor provider can remove revenue and the capitation income that came with it, which weakens cash flow visibility and debt service capacity. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_ach_omi-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 24

Weakness two is operating leverage. Adjusted EBITDA fell 56.40% of lost revenue, the adjusted margin was 7.94% in the third quarter and rental revenue fell 20.00%, so further revenue loss reaches earnings quickly and leverage rises without any new borrowing. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ach_ach-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 9; calculation C09; calculation C11; calculation C31

Weakness three is leverage and cover. Net debt is 8.05x calculated EBITDA, cover is 1.67x and adjusted net leverage is 9.04x on the third-quarter run-rate, which leaves little room for a coupon increase of USD 116.59 million a year on two series. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C05; calculation C10; calculation C12

Weakness four is cash conversion. Free cash flow on the issuer's definition was negative in nine months 2026 and is negative USD 49.79 million at the run-rate after the new coupons and before term loan interest, so liquidity funds the gap and no deleveraging comes from cash generation. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C14

Weakness five is thin equity, listing risk and market pricing of the debt. Equity is a USD 568.23 million deficit under two NYSE notices and the issuer's fair value estimate puts the second lien notes at 36.21% of carrying value, which limits equity as a cushion or a source of new capital and makes another exchange or an equity issue the likely routes if earnings do not recover. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ach_ach-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ach_ach-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 42; calculation C28

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: The sale of the Products & Healthcare Services business to Dominion Healthcare Acquisition Corporation was agreed on 2025-10-07 for USD 375 million in cash, subject to adjustments for cash, debt, working capital and transaction expenses, and completed on 2025-12-31. The company received USD 342 million in cash at closing, recorded a USD 20 million investment for the 5% equity interest it kept, and conveyed USD 18 million of cash with the business, leaving USD 324 million of net proceeds; the purchase price adjustment receivable was about USD 5.0 million at 2026-09-30. The business had net assets of USD 1,037.757 million held for sale at 2024-12-31, so the agreed price is USD 662.757 million below that earlier carrying amount, and the company recorded a USD 798.934 million loss on classifying the business as held for sale during 2025. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ach_omi-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ach_ach-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-K_2025-12-31_ach_omi-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 101; calculation C18; calculation C19

The company reimburses the buyer for 80% of certain separation costs up to USD 65 million, all of which has been incurred, with no payment due before 2026-04-01, none above USD 15 million before 2026-10-01 and none above USD 55 million before 2027-01-01. A transition services agreement runs for up to two years, and the company may have to provide up to USD 115 million of credit support to the sold business through early 2027; none has been required. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ach_ach-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ach_ach-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 13

The Rotech acquisition was agreed on 2024-07-22 for USD 1.36 billion in cash, to be funded with cash and incremental borrowings, and was terminated by mutual agreement on 2025-06-03 with a cash payment of USD 80 million on 2025-06-05. To fund it the company sold USD 1.0 billion of 10.000% senior secured notes due 2030 on 2025-04-04 into escrow, and redeemed them in full at par plus accrued interest on 2025-06-10; the financing fees were USD 18.288 million, and acquisition-related charges were USD 22 million in each of 2024 and 2025. Basis: 10-K_2024-12-31_ach_omi-20241231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-K_2025-12-31_ach_omi-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 63; 10-K_2025-12-31_ach_omi-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 74; 10-K_2025-12-31_ach_omi-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 75; 10-K_2025-12-31_ach_omi-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 81; calculation C20

The Balance Sheet Optimization Transaction of June 2026 is the new debt issue. The company issued 9.000% senior secured first lien notes due 2032 and 9.750% senior secured second lien notes due 2033, guaranteed on a senior secured basis by its existing and future wholly owned domestic subsidiaries; USD 326 million of the new 2032 notes was used to extinguish the Term Loan A. Holders of USD 478 million of 2029 notes and USD 548 million of 2030 notes (about 99.9% and 99.2%) exchanged, leaving USD 0.3 million and USD 4.2 million of unsecured notes that the issuer describes as effectively subordinated; at 2026-09-30 USD 539 million of 2032 notes and USD 698 million of 2033 notes were outstanding, with the first interest payments on 2026-12-15. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ach_ach-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ach_ach-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ach_ach-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 25; calculation C26

On 2026-06-15 the revolving credit agreement was amended to extend its maturity to January 2030, with springing maturities, the earliest in December 2028, and to cut commitments by USD 150 million to USD 300 million; the company announced these steps on 2026-05-11 as commitments from existing creditors. The receivables programme, amended and restated on 2025-12-31 with a USD 150 million limit, was extended on 2026-10-29 from October 2027 to October 2029, a change dated after the quarter end that is not in the 2026-09-30 figures. Basis: 10-Q_2026-03-31_ach_ach-20260331x10q.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ach_ach-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ach_ach-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ach_ach-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 23

The filings do not establish the executed terms of any of these debt instruments, how the revolver, Term Loan B and secured notes rank against each other, how the proceeds of the sale were applied, or who holds the other 95% of the sold business.

fields.value: Financial foundation for Accendra Health Inc/Va/ (ach-75252) as of 2026-11-18 under the credit_snapshot pathway. Scope is the continuing business of Accendra Health, Inc.: FY2024 and FY2025 annual statements, nine-month 2025 and 2026 interim statements, carrying-value debt, liquidity and the last-twelve-months position at 2026-09-30. EBITDA is calculated because the issuer states only an adjusted figure.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Accendra's leverage is high and its earnings base is shrinking: net debt is 8.05x last-twelve-months EBITDA before add-backs and that EBITDA covers cash interest only 1.67x, so creditors depend on the June 2026 refinancing and the revolver, not on cash generation, to carry the turnaround.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage trajectory. At 2026-09-30 carrying-value debt is USD 1,754.966 million and net debt USD 1,728.358 million, which is 8.05x calculated reported EBITDA for the last twelve months and 6.74x on the issuer's adjusted measure. Year-end 2025 net debt was 8.04x reported and 4.72x adjusted, so the adjusted ratio worsened by about two turns while net debt fell only 2.24% (from USD 1,767.887 million), because last-twelve-months adjusted EBITDA is USD 256.252 million against USD 374.847 million for FY2025. The reported ratio looks flat because FY2025 reported EBITDA carried USD 80 million of breakage fee and other one-offs that the last twelve months no longer bear. The risk mechanism is operating, not financial: payor termination removed revenue and collection quality, and debt did not fall with it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Coverage. Calculated reported EBITDA covers cash interest paid 1.67x for the last twelve months (1.63x in FY2025) and adjusted EBITDA 1.99x, with the 9.000% and 9.750% secured notes paying their first coupons on 2026-12-15, so cash interest is likely to rise as the higher coupons on the refinanced notes start to be paid in cash (an inference; the filings give no forecast). The recapture credit that lowers reported interest expense is noncash and amortizes through the life of the secured notes, so accrued interest understates the cash burden. Cash interest paid is consolidated and includes interest on debt once allocated to the sold business, which understates continuing-business cover in FY2025.

fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ach_omi-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 83; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ach_ach-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ach_ach-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ach_ach-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, pages 17–18; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ach_ach-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 30; calculation C11; calculation C24

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash-flow quality. Nine-month 2026 operating cash flow is negative, free cash flow on the issuer's definition is negative, and the management discussion states recurring losses and cash outflows from operations in 2026. Reported cash movement was cushioned by proceeds from equipment sales and a non-core asset sale; equipment sold after the payor termination produced gains inside exit and realignment charges, so some of the reported improvement in investing cash flow is liquidation of the asset base that supported the lost revenue. Strongest contrary evidence is the lower interest paid and the reduction of cash costs in selling, general and administrative expenses, which fell 6.0% in nine months; it would win only if gross margin stabilises as collections recover.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity adequacy. Cash is USD 26.608 million and the undrawn revolver USD 238 million, together 15.08% of total debt; the revolver is the main source because cash fell by USD 255.381 million in nine months while the revolver was repaid. Claims that compete for that liquidity sit outside the debt figure: USD 65 million of reimbursable separation costs to the buyer of the sold business, with payment not required above USD 15 million before 2026-10-01 or above USD 55 million before 2027-01-01, possible credit support of up to USD 115 million under the transition services agreement, an IRS matter with USD 16 million still owed, and operating lease liabilities. No debt matures before 2029 apart from the USD 35 million of revolver borrowings, but a springing maturity could pull the revolver forward to December 2028, and the receivables programme, which funds working capital with USD 136 million sold and uncollected, has a limit of USD 150 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Non-debt funding float. The receivables sale programme and the payable owed to the buyer of the sold business are working-capital funding that behaves like borrowing: both are repaid in cash and neither is in total debt. If the programme were not renewed or its eligible receivables fell with revenue, liquidity would have to come from the revolver, which is limited to USD 238 million. The October 2026 amendment moved the termination date from October 2027 to October 2029, which removes the nearest renewal date.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Data-quality and definition risks. The issuer states no unadjusted EBITDA, so reported EBITDA is calculated from the pre-tax loss, net interest and depreciation and amortization; the FY2024 figure is negative after the goodwill impairment charge, so no FY2024 leverage is stated. Dashes in the statements are carried as missing, the maturity ladder dashes are read as nil, and the Term Loan B principal is printed rounded, so the principal-to-carrying reconciliation relies on that rounded figure for one line.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No unadjusted EBITDA is stated by the issuer, so EBITDA (Reported) in every period is calculated from the pre-tax loss, net interest and depreciation and amortization; this restricts comparison with any covenant EBITDA and is Medium severity; closing it needs the credit agreement's EBITDA definition.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: FY2024 calculated EBITDA is negative after the goodwill impairment charge, so total and net debt to EBITDA for FY2024 are not calculable; this restricts the leverage trend before 2025 and is Low severity; closing it needs no further source because adjusted figures are shown beside it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Covenant levels, step-downs and definitions for the leverage and interest-coverage ratios the revolver and credit agreement require are not printed in any source, so covenant headroom is not calculable; this restricts any covenant conclusion and is High severity; closing it needs the executed credit agreement and amendments.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No source states how the revolver, Term Loan B, first-lien 2032 notes and second-lien 2033 notes rank against one another, so the debt stack groups the first three as one tier and carries the ordering inside it as presentation only; this restricts any priority or recovery use and is High severity; closing it needs the indentures and the intercreditor and security documents.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The Term Loan B principal and the 2029 unsecured notes principal are printed rounded (USD 511 million and USD 0.3 million), so the principal split between them is implied from the ladder; this restricts the per-instrument principal reconciliation by about USD 0.5 million and is Low severity; closing it needs the loan statements.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Margins and floors on the revolver and Term Loan B are stated only as an Applicable Rate defined in the credit agreement, and the interest rate swap was terminated in May 2026, so floating-rate cost cannot be projected from the filings; this restricts interest forecasting and is Medium severity; closing it needs the credit agreements and the current rate.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The statements print dashes for several lines, which are carried as missing rather than zero, the maturity ladder dashes are read as no scheduled principal, and interest income is not stated separately because interest is reported net; this restricts nothing numerically but affects the readers of those cells and is Low severity; closing it needs no source.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue from terminated commercial payor contracts is stated for FY2025 and nine months 2026 only, and last-twelve-months growth, gross margin and interest expense are not constructed, so those cells are not supplied; this restricts trend comparison and is Low severity; closing it needs the quarterly payor disclosure.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash interest paid is consolidated and includes interest on debt that was allocated to the sold business while it was owned, with no split in the sources, so interest cover for FY2024, FY2025 and nine months 2025 is understated for the continuing business; this is Medium severity; closing it needs the interest paid attributable to discontinued operations.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The cash flow statements for FY2024, FY2025 and nine months 2025 are consolidated with discontinued operations on their own lines, so operating cash flow and closing cash are not continuing-business figures; no standard free cash flow is calculated and the issuer's own free cash flow is used; this is Medium severity; closing it needs a continuing-operations cash flow statement.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Maintenance and growth capital expenditure are not separated for patient service equipment and other fixed assets, so a maintenance-capital measure is not calculable; this restricts free cash flow quality and is Low severity; closing it needs management disclosure.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Receivables sold under the programme (USD 136 million uncollected at 2026-09-30), the USD 110 million principal recapture liability, the USD 65 million separation cost payable to the buyer and possible credit support of up to USD 115 million sit outside total debt; they are carried to the analysis as claims outside debt and this is Medium severity; closing it needs the programme and transition agreements.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Only the balance sheets at 2024-12-31, 2025-12-31 and 2026-09-30 and the nine-month and annual statements are tabulated; the first and second quarters of 2026 and the discrete third-quarter cash flow are not, so quarterly cash flow trends are not shown; this is Low severity; closing it needs the 2026 quarterly statements tabulated or an earnings release.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The issuer reports one segment, so no segment profit exists and revenue is shown by product category only; this restricts segment margin analysis and is Low severity; closing it needs management segment data.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No pro forma adjustments exist after 2026-09-30 because the subsequent events state no change in debt; the nearest events, the receivables programme amendment, the chief executive succession and the NYSE notices, are dated and kept out of period figures; this is Low severity.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Business and governance review of Accendra Health Inc/Va/ (ach-75252) as of 2026-11-18 under the credit_snapshot pathway. Scope is the continuing home healthcare business: what it does, who owns and governs it, the transactions and dated events since 2022 that change creditor risk, and the sponsor and governance behaviour the five supplied filings document. No sponsor or controlling holder is identified, so behaviour is read from the issuer's own recorded actions, and the legal capacity behind it is stated as not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Sponsor and governance risk is Medium: no controlling owner or extraction is documented, but equity is a USD 568.23 million deficit under two NYSE notices and a new chief executive started on 2026-10-05, so creditors carry the outcome.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ach_ach-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ach_ach-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ach_ach-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 42; Source readiness (CP-0)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue fell 10.24% in the first nine months of 2026, nearly all of it from commercial payor contracts that were 12% of 2025 revenue. Management paid no dividend and stopped share repurchases, but it paid USD 80 million to end the Rotech acquisition and moved nearly all unsecured notes into secured notes in June 2026. The missing proxy statement and executed debt documents mean this view rests on the filings alone.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ach_ach-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-K_2025-12-31_ach_omi-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 24; 10-K_2025-12-31_ach_omi-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 63; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ach_ach-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 17; calculation C04; calculation C05

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No sponsor or controlling shareholder is identified, so governance risk comes from the issuer's own decisions and from the incentives of an out-of-the-money equity, not from a financial owner's conduct. The common stock is listed and held by record holders, the filings name no parent, and ownership above the share count sits in a proxy statement that was not supplied, so this is a finding that none is documented, not that none exists.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Equity holders have little left to lose, which matters because decisions taken for their benefit would be paid for by creditors. The total deficit is USD 568.23 million, the average market value of the stock stayed below USD 50 million over 30 trading days and the average closing price stayed below USD 1.00. Management plans a reverse split of 1-for-20 to 1-for-30 for the price notice and is still weighing alternatives for the equity notice, whose cure period is 18 months.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: A new chief executive and a new commercial leader arrive after the payor loss, which raises execution risk but keeps board continuity. The new chief executive has been a director since March 2022, the former chief executive left the board and will advise for up to 30 months, and a newly created chief commercial officer joined the same day.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue durability is the main business risk and it is concentrated in a few payors, not spread across products. In 2025 the two largest commercial payors were 23% and 14% of revenue and Medicare and Medicaid 19%, and the terminated commercial contracts were 12% of revenue and nearly all capitation revenue. In the first nine months of 2026 those contracts explain USD 205 million, or about 97.49%, of the decline, while sleep therapy fell 16.2% and home respiratory therapy 14.8%.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ach_omi-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 24; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ach_ach-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 27; calculation C05; calculation C07

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Operating leverage is working against the business: revenue is falling faster than cost, and the cost ratios are rising. Cost of net revenue fell 4.3% against revenue down 10.24%, so it rose to 56.4% of revenue from 52.9%, and selling, general and administrative cost rose to 40.6% of revenue from 38.8%. The issuer attributes the cost ratio to lower collection rates, equipment depreciation fell only 3.3%, and no quantified targets are given for its value creation plan, so the path back to profit is stated but not measured.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ach_ach-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 28; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ach_ach-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 36; calculation C12; calculation C13

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Part of 2026 cash comes from selling assets, which cannot recur at this scale (an inference). In nine months the company received USD 125 million from selling patient service equipment, USD 85 million of it in connection with the payor termination, and USD 33 million from a non-core asset, against capital expenditure of USD 131 million, and it states recurring losses and cash outflows from operations in 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strategy has swung from acquisition to disposal within about 18 months, which makes the plan harder to underwrite and puts weight on the new chief executive's first plan (an inference). The Rotech acquisition for USD 1.36 billion in cash was agreed in July 2024 and ended in June 2025 after a USD 80 million payment, and the sale of Products & Healthcare Services completed on 2025-12-31 for USD 375 million in cash, which is 36.14% of the net assets that were held for sale at the end of 2024.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Creditor treatment in the June 2026 exchange was consensual in form but left holdouts behind, and it is classed as mixed. Holders of 99.9% of the 2029 notes and 99.2% of the 2030 notes tendered into first lien notes due 2032 and second lien notes due 2033 (USD 539 million and USD 698 million outstanding), which moved maturities out and added security at higher coupons; the unsecured notes left, USD 0.3 million and USD 4.2 million, are effectively subordinated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Disclosure quality is a strength for monitoring, with one past accounting error corrected. The auditor gave unqualified opinions on the 2025 statements and on internal control, disclosure controls were judged effective at 2026-09-30, and a USD 21 million over-accrual of accounts payable built up over several years was corrected through opening equity after the issuer judged it not material.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Healthcare programme compliance is a licence-to-operate dependency. Apria's five-year Corporate Integrity Agreement imposes board oversight duties, its closure is expected in 2026, and a breach could bring stipulated penalties or exclusion from federal healthcare programmes.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against a Medium rating is that nothing in the supplied filings shows value leaving for owners. No dividend appears in the statements, repurchases stopped after USD 10.14 million, the exchange was agreed with existing creditors who accepted it almost unanimously, the auditor's opinions on the statements and on internal control are unqualified, and the new chief executive is an existing director, so continuity is likelier than a break. The payor step-down is also complete: the terminated contracts produced revenue only in the first quarter of 2026 and none in the third, and in May 2026 management said it did not expect material effects on operating income from the remaining terminations, so later comparisons lose that drag.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ach_ach-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ach_ach-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ach_ach-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 43; 10-K_2025-12-31_ach_omi-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 79; 10-Q_2026-03-31_ach_ach-20260331x10q.htm.jsonl, page 23; calculation C21

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest case for High is that equity is a deficit, the listing is under notice and the only stated cure for the price notice is a reverse split that needs a shareholder vote, so a restructuring or an equity raise on terms that favour new capital over existing creditors becomes more likely (an inference). The Series C preferred stock and the rights agreement of 2026-08-10 are unexplained in the filings and could change control.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The view would move to High on any of these: a further exchange or lien step that treats holders of the same debt differently, an issue of equity or preferred stock that dilutes or outranks existing creditors, a delisting, covenant waivers without deleveraging, or a payment to shareholders. It would move to Low only on evidence not supplied: a proxy statement showing an independent board and no dominant holder, executed debt documents with tight restricted payment limits, and a quantified plan whose first results show revenue and the cost ratios stabilising.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The proxy statement was not supplied, so holders above five percent, board independence and committees, and any shareholder agreement are not established; this keeps the finding of no identified controlling owner at not documented and holds the Medium risk level below a firmer rating.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The terms of the Series C preferred stock and the rights agreement of 2026-08-10 are not stated, so whether they dilute or outrank existing holders, or protect tax assets, is not established; this could move the control and creditor alignment findings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Payor shares are stated for 2025 only, and the revenue still earned from the payor that ended contracts is not stated, so the durability finding cannot say how much of the remaining revenue depends on that payor; it holds only for the part already lost.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The issuer gives no quantified targets for its value creation plan, so the finding that cost ratios are worsening cannot be tested against management's expected recovery; it stays a description of the first nine months of 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No executed credit agreement or indenture was supplied, so the capacity to pay dividends, make investments, grant liens or move assets is not established; the finding that no extraction is documented describes behaviour only and says nothing on what the documents allow.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Each behaviour, an abandoned acquisition, a disposal and an exchange offer, appears once in the filings, so no pattern is inferred; acquisition appetite and creditor treatment stay at mixed and are not read as tendencies.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The sale of the Products & Healthcare Services business to Dominion Healthcare Acquisition Corporation was agreed on 2025-10-07 for USD 375 million in cash, subject to adjustments for cash, debt, working capital and transaction expenses, and completed on 2025-12-31. The company received USD 342 million in cash at closing, recorded a USD 20 million investment for the 5% equity interest it kept, and conveyed USD 18 million of cash with the business, leaving USD 324 million of net proceeds; the purchase price adjustment receivable was about USD 5.0 million at 2026-09-30. The business had net assets of USD 1,037.757 million held for sale at 2024-12-31, so the agreed price is USD 662.757 million below that earlier carrying amount, and the company recorded a USD 798.934 million loss on classifying the business as held for sale during 2025.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The company reimburses the buyer for 80% of certain separation costs up to USD 65 million, all of which has been incurred, with no payment due before 2026-04-01, none above USD 15 million before 2026-10-01 and none above USD 55 million before 2027-01-01. A transition services agreement runs for up to two years, and the company may have to provide up to USD 115 million of credit support to the sold business through early 2027; none has been required.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The Rotech acquisition was agreed on 2024-07-22 for USD 1.36 billion in cash, to be funded with cash and incremental borrowings, and was terminated by mutual agreement on 2025-06-03 with a cash payment of USD 80 million on 2025-06-05. To fund it the company sold USD 1.0 billion of 10.000% senior secured notes due 2030 on 2025-04-04 into escrow, and redeemed them in full at par plus accrued interest on 2025-06-10; the financing fees were USD 18.288 million, and acquisition-related charges were USD 22 million in each of 2024 and 2025.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The Balance Sheet Optimization Transaction of June 2026 is the new debt issue. The company issued 9.000% senior secured first lien notes due 2032 and 9.750% senior secured second lien notes due 2033, guaranteed on a senior secured basis by its existing and future wholly owned domestic subsidiaries; USD 326 million of the new 2032 notes was used to extinguish the Term Loan A. Holders of USD 478 million of 2029 notes and USD 548 million of 2030 notes (about 99.9% and 99.2%) exchanged, leaving USD 0.3 million and USD 4.2 million of unsecured notes that the issuer describes as effectively subordinated; at 2026-09-30 USD 539 million of 2032 notes and USD 698 million of 2033 notes were outstanding, with the first interest payments on 2026-12-15.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: On 2026-06-15 the revolving credit agreement was amended to extend its maturity to January 2030, with springing maturities, the earliest in December 2028, and to cut commitments by USD 150 million to USD 300 million; the company announced these steps on 2026-05-11 as commitments from existing creditors. The receivables programme, amended and restated on 2025-12-31 with a USD 150 million limit, was extended on 2026-10-29 from October 2027 to October 2029, a change dated after the quarter end that is not in the 2026-09-30 figures.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The filings do not establish the executed terms of any of these debt instruments, how the revolver, Term Loan B and secured notes rank against each other, how the proceeds of the sale were applied, or who holds the other 95% of the sold business.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Module status: Ready with Limitations, because the filings support the business, transaction and behaviour findings but no proxy statement, executed debt documents or management guidance were supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The risk level is Medium, driven by an equity deficit under two listing notices and a documented exchange that left holdouts behind, because equity incentives and subordination can move value away from existing creditors, which implies weaker priority for unsecured claims and a need to monitor any equity or preferred issue. Countervailing evidence is no dividend, stopped repurchases, clean audit opinions and an exchange accepted by nearly all holders. Further analysis requires the proxy statement, the executed debt documents and quantified plan targets.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Sponsor / Governance Risk Level: Medium. The nine scoring dimensions are not scored because fewer than four are evidence-supported without a sponsor, so no composite score is stated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Seven gaps are open, two of them material. None stops the business or governance findings, but the first two limit how far the governance and revenue findings can be pushed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Ownership above the share count, board independence and committees, shareholder agreements and executive pay are not supplied because Part III is incorporated from the 2026 proxy statement; this limits the ownership and governance findings and the risk level, is Material, and closing it needs the 2026 proxy statement and the current reports filed in August and September 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue still earned from the payor that terminated contracts, and the payor mix in 2026, are not stated, because payor shares are given for 2025 only; this limits the revenue durability finding and the operating model, is Material, and closing it needs payor mix by quarter or management disclosure.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The terms of the Series C Cumulative Preferred Stock and the Section 382 Rights Agreement of 2026-08-10, and whether any preferred stock was issued, are not stated; this limits the ownership and creditor alignment findings, is Minor, and closing it needs the current report of 2026-08-10 and its exhibits.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The value creation plan is described but no savings, revenue or timing targets are stated; this limits the margin outlook, is Minor, and closing it needs management guidance, earnings releases and presentations.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Executed credit agreements and indentures were not supplied, so capacity for restricted payments, investments, debt, liens and asset transfers is not established; this limits the legal-capacity link in the behaviour flags, is Minor, and closing it needs the executed documents and amendments.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Compensation, related-party dealings and the terms of the consulting agreement with the former chief executive are not supplied; this limits the governance register, is Minor, and closing it needs the proxy statement and the current report of 2026-09-28.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Holders of the other 95% of the sold business and the rights attached to the retained 5% interest are not stated; this limits the view of the counterparty behind the separation cost and transition obligations, is Minor, and closing it needs the equity purchase agreement.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fundamental credit assessment of Accendra Health Inc/Va/ (ach-75252) as of 2026-11-18 under the credit_snapshot pathway. Scope is the continuing home healthcare business to 2026-09-30: business quality, financial profile, liquidity, refinancing capacity, governance and the main downside path, built on the three supplied analyses and checked against the five filings. It gives no rating, security recommendation, legal-capacity conclusion or position size.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Accendra's fundamental credit profile is weak: net debt is 8.05x calculated EBITDA, cash interest cover is 1.67x and the third-quarter earnings run-rate is below the last twelve months, so creditors depend on the 2026 refinancing, the revolver and asset sales, not on cash generation.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ach_ach-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 31; calculation C01; calculation C05

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity covers the next year, with no maturity before 2029 except USD 35 million of revolver borrowings, but fixed coupons on the two secured note series alone will cost USD 116.59 million a year from 2026-12-15, and the issuer's own fair value estimate puts the second lien notes at 36.21% of carrying value. Top risk: the loss of a second large payor relationship, because the first loss took 56.40% of lost revenue out of adjusted EBITDA.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ach_ach-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ach_ach-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ach_ach-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 18; calculation C11; calculation C12; calculation C28

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage is high and rising on current earnings. Net debt is 8.05x calculated reported EBITDA and 6.74x issuer-adjusted EBITDA for the last twelve months, against 4.72x adjusted at the end of 2025, and 9.04x on adjusted EBITDA annualised from the third quarter. Net debt fell only 2.24% since 2025-12-31 while adjusted EBITDA fell 41.64% in nine months.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ach_ach-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 31; calculation C01; calculation C05; calculation C09; calculation C10; calculation C26

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash interest is about to step up. The 2032 first lien and 2033 second lien notes pay their first coupons on 2026-12-15 and carry USD 116.59 million of fixed cash interest a year, which is 90.55% of the cash interest paid on all debt in the last twelve months, while interest paid in the third quarter was 64.15% lower than a year earlier because the first coupons on the new notes fall after the quarter (an inference). At the third-quarter run-rate, issuer-defined free cash flow before interest paid is USD 66.81 million a year, so after those coupons it is negative USD 49.79 million, before any interest on the term loan and revolver.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ach_ach-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ach_ach-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ach_ach-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 31; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ach_ach-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 32; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C12; calculation C13; calculation C14; calculation C15

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Debt investors already price distress at the junior tier. The issuer's own estimated fair value of total debt is 68.53% of carrying value, the first lien notes due 2032 are at 88.29%, the Term Loan B at 90.28% and the second lien notes due 2033 at 36.21% (35.81% of principal), which suggests a market view of high default risk that the carrying-value ratios do not show (an inference). On the estimated fair value of debt, net leverage would be 5.48x calculated EBITDA, a sensitivity and not the primary ratio.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ach_ach-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ach_ach-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 16; calculation C28; calculation C29

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue durability is the weakest business factor. Two commercial payors were 23% and 14% of 2025 revenue, the terminated contracts were 12% and explain 97.49% of the nine-month decline of 10.24%, and the same payor still accounted for about 11 percentage points of 2025 revenue outside the terminated contracts (an inference from rounded shares). The underlying trend is milder: the issuer's listed drivers outside the terminated contracts and a sold non-core asset sum to a third-quarter decline of 1.06%, and revenue from Medicare grew 4.87% while commercial payor revenue fell 13.52% and capitation revenue fell 78.02%.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_ach_omi-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 24; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ach_ach-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ach_ach-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ach_ach-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 27; calculation C16; calculation C17; calculation C30; calculation C32

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Margins fall faster than costs can be cut. Adjusted EBITDA fell by 56.40% of the revenue lost in nine months 2026, the adjusted margin was 7.94% in the third quarter against 13.22% a year earlier, and cost of net revenue rose to 56.4% of revenue from 52.9% because equipment depreciation is largely fixed and collection rates are lower; rental revenue fell 20.00% while equipment depreciation fell only 3.3%, so depreciation rose to 22.59% of rental revenue from 18.68%.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ach_ach-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ach_ach-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 28; calculation C09; calculation C11; calculation C27; calculation C31

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity is adequate for twelve months but thin against the debt. Cash and the undrawn revolver are 15.08% of total debt and cover the run-rate free cash flow shortfall several times before term loan interest, no debt falls due before 2029 except the revolver borrowings, and the receivables programme runs to October 2029, but USD 311 million of claims sit outside total debt and the programme is 90.67% used.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ach_ach-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 37; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ach_ach-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 38; calculation C08; calculation C14; calculation C19; calculation C20; calculation C34

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Refinancing capacity depends on stabilising earnings before the 2028 and 2029 dates. The Term Loan B of USD 511 million falls due in March 2029, the revolver can spring forward to December 2028, and the secured notes due in 2032 and 2033 are 69.21% of contractual principal, so the next refinancing will be tested against the third-quarter run-rate, not the 2025 results. Equity is a USD 568.23 million deficit under two NYSE notices and goodwill is 59.08% of total assets, which narrows the alternatives to another exchange or an equity issue.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ach_ach-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ach_ach-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ach_ach-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ach_ach-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 37; calculation C18; calculation C21; calculation C33

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Governance adds risk but not extraction. Business & governance rates sponsor and governance risk Medium: no dividend, repurchases stopped, nearly all unsecured notes exchanged into secured notes, a new chief executive from 2026-10-05 and no controlling holder identified.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: A second payor loss is the downside that would break the credit. Losing revenue equal to the 14% payor share at the observed flow-through would remove about USD 218.09 million from adjusted EBITDA and leave cash and the revolver covering about 11.9 months of the resulting cash burn before any management action (an illustrative sensitivity, not a forecast).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C11; calculation C22; calculation C23

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence for a better view is that the payor step-down is finished and the earnings base can be measured. The terminated contracts produced revenue only in the first quarter of 2026, the third quarter had none, management said in May 2026 that it did not expect material operating income effects from the remaining terminations, and selling, general and administrative cost already fell 6.0%. Categories that grew or held, diabetes, ostomy and urology, are 45.16% of nine-month revenue, no debt matures before 2029 except USD 35 million, the covenants were met at 2026-09-30 and management states that cash and the revolver will meet its cash needs.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-03-31_ach_ach-20260331x10q.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ach_ach-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ach_ach-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ach_ach-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 28; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ach_ach-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 36; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ach_ach-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 38; calculation C24

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The view would improve if fourth-quarter revenue held above the third-quarter level with adjusted margin above 7.94%, if interest paid after 2026-12-15 stayed inside issuer-defined free cash flow, and if covenant levels, once supplied, showed headroom above the current ratios. It would worsen on any further payor termination, on a covenant waiver, on the revolver being drawn to cover interest, or on an equity or preferred issue that dilutes or outranks creditors.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Covenant levels, step-downs and definitions are not supplied, so the liquidity finding assumes the stated compliance continues; a breach would put the USD 238 million of revolver availability at risk and move the liquidity assessment from average to weak.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Margins and floors on the Term Loan B and the revolver are not stated, so interest after 2026-12-15 is quantified only for the two secured note series; the free cash flow run-rate is therefore an upper bound.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The payor that ended contracts is not named and the 2026 shares of the two largest payors are not stated, although revenue by payor type is, so the 11 percentage points of 2025 revenue still tied to it are an inference and the second payor sensitivity rests on a 2025 share of 14%.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No agency ratings, dated market quotes or peer data were supplied beyond the issuer's own fair value estimates, so the weak profile is judged on the issuer's own trend and not against comparable issuers.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The third-quarter run-rate multiplies one quarter by four, and the filings state that third and fourth quarters usually carry higher volume, so the run-rate figures are indicative and could understate a full year of seasonal weakness in other quarters.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strength one is a maturity profile with no near-term wall. The 2029 maturities are USD 511.338 million, the secured notes mature in 2032 and 2033, and only the USD 35 million of revolver borrowings fall due before 2029, so refinancing risk before then is limited to the springing revolver date.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ach_ach-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 18; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C18

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strength two is liquidity that can fund a year of base-case needs. Cash plus the undrawn revolver are 15.08% of total debt and the receivables programme was extended to October 2029, which lowers the chance of a funding gap before earnings stabilise.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ach_ach-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 23; calculation C08

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strength three is a category base that is stable. Diabetes, ostomy and urology were 45.16% of nine-month revenue and grew or held while sleep therapy and home respiratory therapy absorbed the payor loss, so the revenue floor is higher than the headline decline suggests.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strength four is reporting that lets creditors monitor. The auditor gave unqualified opinions, disclosure controls were effective at 2026-09-30 and dated events are disclosed, which supports early warning from the triggers below.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strength five is a cost response already under way. Selling, general and administrative cost fell 6.0% and payor transitions were completed in the first half of 2026, so the base is visible.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weakness one is payor concentration. Two commercial payors were 23% and 14% of 2025 revenue and the terminated contracts were 12%, so one decision by a buyer with a successor provider can remove revenue and the capitation income that came with it, which weakens cash flow visibility and debt service capacity.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weakness two is operating leverage. Adjusted EBITDA fell 56.40% of lost revenue, the adjusted margin was 7.94% in the third quarter and rental revenue fell 20.00%, so further revenue loss reaches earnings quickly and leverage rises without any new borrowing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ach_ach-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 9; calculation C09; calculation C11; calculation C31

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weakness three is leverage and cover. Net debt is 8.05x calculated EBITDA, cover is 1.67x and adjusted net leverage is 9.04x on the third-quarter run-rate, which leaves little room for a coupon increase of USD 116.59 million a year on two series.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C05; calculation C10; calculation C12

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weakness four is cash conversion. Free cash flow on the issuer's definition was negative in nine months 2026 and is negative USD 49.79 million at the run-rate after the new coupons and before term loan interest, so liquidity funds the gap and no deleveraging comes from cash generation.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weakness five is thin equity, listing risk and market pricing of the debt. Equity is a USD 568.23 million deficit under two NYSE notices and the issuer's fair value estimate puts the second lien notes at 36.21% of carrying value, which limits equity as a cushion or a source of new capital and makes another exchange or an equity issue the likely routes if earnings do not recover.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ach_ach-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ach_ach-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 42; calculation C28

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Accendra is a single-segment home healthcare provider that rents equipment and sells supplies to patients and home health agencies under the Apria and Byram Healthcare brands, and it sold Products & Healthcare Services on 2025-12-31 for USD 375 million in cash. Revenue comes from fee-for-service and capitation arrangements with government and commercial payors, and the company says it supports patients over the life of their therapy, which gives some visibility, but the terminated commercial contracts removed nearly all capitation revenue and showed that visibility depends on a few payors. The sale reduced diversification, as the 2025 annual report itself says, so debt service now rests on one business whose reimbursement is set by payors and regulators, which weakens cash-flow visibility and refinancing confidence.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_ach_omi-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-K_2025-12-31_ach_omi-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 32; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ach_ach-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 37

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Accendra is a listed Virginia corporation with no sponsor, parent or controlling holder identified in the supplied filings; the proxy statement that would show holders above 5% was not supplied. The notes issued in June 2026 are guaranteed on a senior secured basis by existing and future wholly owned domestic subsidiaries, a receivables subsidiary sells receivables to the programme, and non-guarantor subsidiaries and any restricted or unrestricted group designation are not identified, so structural seniority cannot be assessed here. Leverage tolerance is shown by the abandoned Rotech acquisition for USD 1.36 billion and by the use of an exchange to extend maturities; the filings show no dividend and stopped repurchases, so the creditor risk lies in strategy reversals, listing pressure and the new chief executive rather than in distributions.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ach_ach-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ach_ach-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 17; Source readiness (CP-0)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue is partly recurring because patients stay on therapy, but it is concentrated, regulated and exposed to substitution by a payor's choice of provider. In 2025 two commercial payors were 23% and 14% of revenue, Medicare and Medicaid 19%, and the largest payor ended contracts worth 12% of revenue, with a successor provider taking over the patients; the Medicare competitive bidding programme re-bids contracts at least every three years, and a June 2025 coverage determination can make qualifying for home ventilation harder. Price and volume are not separated in the filings and no pass-through mechanism is stated, so pricing power is not established; the evidence of buyer power is the contract loss itself, which lowers revenue visibility and the quality of cash flow available for debt service.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_ach_omi-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-K_2025-12-31_ach_omi-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 24; 10-K_2025-12-31_ach_omi-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 28; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ach_ach-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 37

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Costs fall more slowly than revenue. In nine months 2026 revenue fell 10.24% while cost of net revenue fell 4.3%, patient service equipment depreciation fell 3.3% and selling, general and administrative cost fell 6.0%, so margin cannot be defended under volume loss without further action; the issuer also notes that volume-based supplier discounts depend on order volumes, so falling volume can raise unit cost. Stranded costs from the sold business remain in continuing operations and in Adjusted EBITDA, and net fees under the transition services agreement were USD 26 million in nine months 2026, which will fall as services are replaced; this supports partial margin recovery but is not quantified by the issuer.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ach_ach-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ach_ach-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 28; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ach_ach-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 31; 10-K_2025-12-31_ach_omi-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 28; calculation C09

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Equipment spending is the main cash call: capital expenditure was USD 131 million in nine months 2026 against USD 153 million, a cut of 14.38%, and equipment and asset sales raised USD 125 million and USD 33 million, so part of 2026 cash flow is a sale of the asset base. Free cash flow on the issuer's definition was positive in 2025 and negative in nine months 2026, working capital is managed with a receivables programme where one day of collection is about USD 6.5 million, and USD 65 million of separation costs are payable to the buyer of the sold business. EBITDA converts to free cash flow only while interest is low; with fixed coupons of USD 116.59 million on the two secured series from 2026-12-15 the conversion turns negative at the run-rate, and capex flexibility is the main lever (the filings give no maintenance and growth split).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ach_ach-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ach_ach-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 35; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ach_ach-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ach_ach-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 32; calculation C12; calculation C14

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Rivalry is high: national and regional providers and pharmacy benefit managers compete for the same payor contracts, and the loss of a payor's volume to a successor provider is direct evidence. Buyer power is high because payors are concentrated and set reimbursement, supplier power is meaningful because the three largest suppliers were about 40% of purchases and a supplier recall affected 2024 results, and the filings state no evidence on new entrants or substitutes beyond pharmacy benefit managers, so those forces are not established. The credit consequence is limited pricing power and margin exposure to payor and supplier terms.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Regulation is a primary credit driver because reimbursement under Medicare and Medicaid, competitive bidding and a June 2025 coverage determination for home ventilation set revenue and volume in the categories that fell most, and a breach of Apria's Corporate Integrity Agreement could cost penalties or programme exclusion. Economic factors matter through floating-rate debt, since the Term Loan B and the revolver carry a spread over a benchmark rate and the margin is not stated; social and technology factors do not appear to be primary credit drivers in the provided materials.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths are the 2029 to 2033 maturity profile, liquidity of 15.08% of total debt, a base of stable categories and clean reporting. Weaknesses are payor concentration, falling margins, 8.05x leverage and an equity deficit. Opportunities that could improve credit quality are growth in sleep therapy outside the terminated contracts, completion of the cost plan, the end of the Corporate Integrity Agreement and the removal of transition costs. Threats are a second payor loss, further reimbursement changes in Medicare competitive bidding or coverage rules, a covenant breach with cross-default, and a listing failure.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ach_ach-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ach_ach-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 38; calculation C08

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Scale and market position is Average: revenue is USD 2,551.756 million over the last twelve months and the company is a national provider, but market share is not stated. Competitive advantage is Weak because a payor moved volume to a successor provider and no switching-cost evidence is stated. Business diversification is Weak because the company has one segment, two payors were 37% of 2025 revenue and the sale reduced diversification. Cost and capex flexibility is Average because capex fell and selling, general and administrative cost fell 6.0%, but equipment depreciation is largely fixed. Margin stability is Weak because the adjusted margin fell to 9.02% in nine months from 13.87%. Free cash flow stability is Weak because it turned negative and the new coupons make it negative at the run-rate. Ability to refinance and access capital markets is Weak because the June 2026 exchange was agreed with existing creditors at higher coupons, the issuer's fair value estimate puts the second lien notes at 36.21% of carrying value and equity is under listing notice. Liquidity position is Average because the next year is covered but liquidity is 15.08% of total debt. Financial policy and governance is Average because no extraction is documented but strategy has reversed twice and risk is Medium.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ach_ach-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 31; calculation C08; calculation C09

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The main supports are the maturity profile and liquidity; the main constraints are payor concentration, leverage and the interest step-up; the trend is down on earnings and flat on debt; the missing data are covenant levels, term loan interest margins, the 2026 payor mix and any management targets.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over 12 to 24 months the base case is revenue near the third-quarter level of USD 601.775 million a quarter with seasonally higher third and fourth quarters, a cost plan that narrows the margin gap only partly, cash interest rising from 2026-12-15 and free cash flow negative before term loan interest at the run-rate; the revolver and cash would fund that gap, so liquidity pressure builds through 2027 without a recovery in adjusted EBITDA (an inference). Over three to five years the 2029 Term Loan B maturity of USD 511 million and the springing revolver date of December 2028 are the test, and a refinancing then depends on adjusted EBITDA recovering from the third-quarter run-rate. Tailwinds are growth in sleep therapy outside the terminated contracts, the end of transition costs and an extended receivables programme; headwinds are payor concentration, Medicare competitive bidding, the coverage determination for home ventilation and the listing notices.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ach_ach-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ach_ach-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ach_ach-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 37; calculation C13; calculation C14

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The initiating condition is a second payor ending contracts, and the sensitivity uses the 14% payor share of 2025 revenue, about USD 386.684 million. The first operational break is volume: equipment depreciation and supplier discounts do not fall with revenue. Using the flow-through seen in nine months 2026, adjusted EBITDA would fall by about USD 218.09 million to about USD 38.16 million, which is below the USD 128.757 million of cash interest paid in the last twelve months. Free cash flow on the issuer's definition would move from about negative USD 49.79 million to about negative USD 267.88 million a year, before term loan and revolver interest, and cash plus the undrawn revolver would cover about 11.9 months of that burn, before management lowers capex, sells equipment, accelerates collections or uses the receivables programme, and before any covenant waiver. The observable triggers are a payor notice, a fall in quarterly revenue below USD 601.775 million, a drawn revolver rising above USD 35 million and a covenant waiver request; resilience looks sufficient to avoid distress in the base case but not in this case without those levers (an illustrative sensitivity).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C11; calculation C22; calculation C23

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, Accendra presents a weak business profile supported by a clear maturity profile, USD 238 million of revolver availability and stable categories, but credit quality is constrained by payor concentration, falling margins, 8.05x leverage and an interest step-up of USD 116.59 million a year on two series. Cash-flow durability appears weak because free cash flow was negative in nine months 2026 and turns more negative after 2026-12-15 at the run-rate. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on adjusted EBITDA recovering before the December 2028 revolver date and the March 2029 Term Loan B maturity. The primary downside path is the loss of a second large payor relationship. Further analysis would require covenant levels, term loan margins, the 2026 payor mix and management targets. Top risk: the loss of a second large commercial payor relationship.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C12; calculation C14

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Module status: Ready with Limitations, because covenant levels, term loan margins, the 2026 payor mix, ratings and management targets were not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Six gaps are open, two of them material. None blocks the credit view, but the first two limit how far the liquidity and revenue findings can be pushed, and three statements of earlier analyses are corrected at the end of this section.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Covenant levels, step-downs and definitions for the leverage and interest coverage tests are not in the filings, so headroom is not calculable; this limits the liquidity and leverage findings, is Material, and closing it needs the executed credit agreement and amendments.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The 2026 shares of the two largest commercial payors and the revenue still earned from the terminating payor are not stated, although revenue by payor type is, so the durability finding and the second payor sensitivity rest on 2025 shares; this limits the revenue and downside findings, is Material, and closing it needs payor concentration by quarter.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Margins and floors on the Term Loan B and the revolver are not stated, so total interest after 2026-12-15 is not calculable; this limits the cash flow finding to the two secured note series, is Minor, and closing it needs the credit agreements.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Management gives no quantified targets for its value creation plan and no forecast, so the outlook is analyst inference; this limits the outlook and margin recovery view, is Minor, and closing it needs guidance or earnings materials.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No agency ratings, dated market quotes or peers were supplied beyond the issuer's own fair value estimates, so relative standing is not assessed; this limits the business profile comparison, is Minor, and closing it needs those inputs.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The actual application of the sale proceeds is not itemised, although the first-quarter 2026 report states that the company anticipated repaying the revolver with them; this limits the view that debt reduction came from the sale, is Minor, and closing it needs a cash flow bridge.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Three statements in the earlier analyses are corrected here. Business & governance says the use of the sale proceeds is not stated, but the first-quarter 2026 report states the anticipated repayment of the revolver; it says the 2026 payor mix is not stated, but the third quarter report gives revenue by payor type, with Medicare plus Medicaid at 22.33% of nine-month revenue; and it reads the June 2026 exchange as lowering refinancing risk for participants, but the debt note shows the second lien notes issued in it at 35.81% of principal, so the company's maturity risk fell while investors in that tranche hold paper priced at a deep discount. Financial foundation does not record the fair value of debt, which this analysis adds.
